extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO OED counsel, and parties in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative decision applying USPTO professional-responsibility rules (37 C.F.R. Parts 10 and 11) to a respondent in an OED disciplinary proceeding; identifies alleged violations, findings of fact, applicable rules, and sanctioning criteria in a default-case context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of failure to answer Complaint (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Failure to timely file an answer will constitute an admission of the allegations in the complaint and may result in entry of default judgment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent does not answer by the deadline, allegations are deemed admitted and the court may enter default judgment; procedural requirement for answering (Notice of Hearing and Order set answer deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify client of Office correspondence (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a), 10.23(b) via 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must inform a client of correspondence received from the Office when the correspondence could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, is received by the practitioner on behalf of a client, and is correspondence which a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifying client timely of Notices to File Missing Parts and similar correspondence is required; failing to inform client of such correspondence is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of legal matter (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes neglecting a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: failing to file entrusted patent applications, failing to remit required filing fees, failing to respond to Office notices; pattern of inaction constitutes neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to seek lawful objectives (37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes intentionally failing to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to take action to protect statutory rights (e.g., not completing or timely completing patent filings before statutory deadlines) violates this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to carry out contract of employment (37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes intentionally failing to carry out a contract of employment entered into with a client for professional services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting payment to perform filings and then not completing or submitting required components (fees, oaths/declarations, filings) constitutes breach of employment contract and a rule violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes timely remittance of statutory filing fees and prompt completion of filings; inaction after notices that applications are incomplete breaches this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keeping client reasonably informed (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must disclose receipt of Office notices and the true status of filings when the client inquires; assuring client filings are "on schedule" when they are not is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt delivery of client funds and accounting (37 C.F.R. § 11.115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to promptly deliver to a client funds that the client is entitled to receive, and failure to promptly render a full accounting upon request by the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a practitioner receives client funds for specific purposes (e.g., USPTO filing fees) and does not remit them or return them when not used, and fails to provide an accounting, this rule is violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of unearned advance payments upon termination (37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to refund advance payment of fees or expenses that have not been earned or incurred upon termination of the practitioner-client relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representation terminates, unearned filing fees or unearned attorney fees must be returned or otherwise accounted for; failure to refund can support discipline and condition reinstatement on restitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices to File Missing Parts — timing and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices to File Missing Parts inform that required fees and inventor's oath/declaration must be timely submitted within two months from the date of the Notice to avoid abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must respond to Notices to File Missing Parts within the stated period or the application will be abandoned; failure to timely respond is actionable neglect and can prejudice client rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to withdraw when attorney-client relationship terminates (37 C.F.R. § 1.36(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must withdraw as attorney of record following termination when required by rule; failure to withdraw may result in continued official correspondence being sent to the practitioner's address of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If practitioner fails to withdraw after termination, Office will continue to communicate to practitioner's address of record; failure to withdraw can compound misconduct by blocking client access to notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiduciary duty when accepting client prepayments
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who accepts prepayment of attorney fees and filing fees has a fiduciary duty to the client with respect to those funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiduciary obligations include remitting client-designated funds (e.g., filing fees) to their intended use, providing accountings, and returning unearned funds promptly; keeping prepaid fees without remitting/returning constitutes breach and aggravating misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of default findings as admissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When respondent defaults by failing to answer or appear, the allegations in the complaint are deemed admitted and can be the basis for findings of fact and conclusions of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default status means the court treats the complaint's factual allegations as true for purposes of establishing violations and determining sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning framework (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sanctioning a practitioner, the Court must consider: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty owed to client/public/system/profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of actual or potential injury caused by the misconduct; and (4) the existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggravating factors cited include multiple violations, a pattern of misconduct, selfish or dishonest motive, failure to make restitution, and failure to appear. Mitigating factors may include lack of prior disciplinary record but may be outweighed by aggravation. Considerable actual or potential client injury supports more severe sanctions (e.g., exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Available sanctions and reinstatement conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions include exclusion from practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office in patent, trademark, and other matters; reinstatement petitions are governed by 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 and may be conditioned on restitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision may exclude practitioner from practice and inform respondent of appeal rights (37 C.F.R. § 11.55(a)) and responsibilities during suspension/exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.58). Reinstatement can require making restitution to harmed clients.
